articleTitle: Impact of Different Parameters on Symmetry and Size of Single Step Anodization Nanopores in Porous Alumina
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Nanoporous Alumina is used widespread as a template material for nano scaled objects since mid-20th century. These nano scaled objects are in the form of nanowires, nanotubes and nanodots etc. In order to synthesize nanoporous alumina, two step anodization techniques has been reported. We have prepared porous alumina with the distinction that arrays of pores in alumina were created by single step anodization. We fabricate nanoporous alumina in 0.3 M oxalic acid for various anodization times at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$23^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> under constant voltage of 40 v. EDX graphs revealed that oxide layer of aluminum was formed on the metal surface of aluminum. SEM micrographs however, depicted a good estimate of pore symmetry under low temperature and resulted in small pores as compared to room temperature. Longer anodization time deepens the pores' depth, whereas at room temperature the acid invaded pores' wall. SEM images made the evident that the sample anodized sporadically has lower degree of pore symmetry than continuously anodized sample. It was also observed that at voltage other than self-ordering i.e. at 60 V, hexagonal symmetry of pores decreases.

articleTitle: Smart Muscle Guardian: A Wearable Device for Real-Time Monitoring of Muscle Fatigue
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: In this paper, a wearable gadget is developed that can assess muscle tiredness in real-time by using an Electromyography (EMG) sensor. It is designed to detect muscle fatigue levels accurately, ensuring safety by alerting users to potential risks during intense physical activities. The Arduino UNO Microcontroller board is used to collect data from the muscle using an EMG sensor and to sound an alarm when muscle activity surpasses a pre-set threshold. The project aims to provide a practical solution for early intervention in emergencies and ongoing monitoring of muscle functionality. An implementation of the proposed device has potential application in improving individual health and reducing the risk of injuries.

articleTitle: Materials Classification via Piezoelectric Sensors for Robotic Grippers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Robotic arms are gradually becoming applicable in every industry. A majority of these are employed in the sorting and identification of objects at assembly lines. Therefore, there is a need for accurate, sensitive, and efficient sensing mechanisms installed on the robotic arm. This research presents an efficient mechanism by using piezoelectric sensors mounted on the robotic gripper. The sensors help in the identification and categorization of objects based on their hardness. The proposed system successfully achieved an average accuracy of 80% over the categorization of three different specimens including hard (wood), intermediate (thermopole), and soft (sponge) materials.

articleTitle: Enhancing Rehabilitation for Frozen Shoulder With a Two-Degree of Freedom Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Frozen shoulder, also known as Adhesive Capsulitis (AC), is characterized by shoulder joint pain and restricted movement caused by capsule inflammation, which is frequently associated with injury, surgery, or illnesses such as diabetes. Current therapies, such as corticosteroid injections and rehabilitation exercises, have disadvantages, with injections being uncomfortable and potentially producing long-term damage, and rehab sessions commonly missed due to logistical difficulties. This research provides a remedy for AC using 2-degree of freedom (DOF) workout equipment designed specifically for the indigenous population to assist in executing critical rehab activities. Our results reveal that for flexion, the average angle at high speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$101.94^{\circ}\pm 11.26^{\circ}$</tex> and at low speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$103.10^{\circ}\pm 8.52^{\circ}$</tex>. For extension, the high-speed average was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$64.53^{\circ}\pm 14.42^{\circ}$</tex> and low speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$65.03^{\circ}\pm 14.06^{\circ}$</tex>. In abduction, the high-speed average was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$102.91^{\circ}\pm 6.84^{\circ}$</tex> and the low-speed average was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$102.56^{\circ}\pm 9.12^{\circ}$</tex>. For adduction, high-speed had an average of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$72.15^{\circ}\pm 13.70^{\circ}$</tex> and low speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$65.03^{\circ}\pm 14.06^{\circ}$</tex>. Thus, patients can utilize it independently or with physiotherapists, which will help reduce sessions and ensure effective exercise application at home.

articleTitle: Analysis of Posture Influence on Memory Using fNIRS-BCI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This study explores the impact of three varied body postures-sitting, standing, and upper-body movement on human memory using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) based brain- computer interface (BCI). The study involves two distinct cognitive activities i.e., the mental arithmetic and picture recall activity. The fNIRS brain signals from 10 healthy subjects (5 male and 5 female) were recorded, and pre-processed. After extracting features, supervised learning was used for classification to analyze how altering body postures affects the memory The Gaussian Naïve Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) classifiers were applied. For the Mental Arithmetic Activity, sitting posture emerged as the optimal posture, demonstrating the maximum achieved accuracy of 84.2%. Conversely, for the Picture Recall Activity, the upper-body movement emerged as the optimal posture, achieving the maximum accuracy of 87.4%. Through comprehensive analysis, this research contributes insights into the intricate relationship between body postures and cognitive functions.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Model Degradation in PaddleOCR, UltOCR, and TrOCR Across Baseline and TensorFlow Lite Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) models are deployed on edge devices for many applications ranging from document scanning to real-time text recognition. For edge deployment, it is suitable to convert OCR models to TensorFlow Lite (TFLite) format. However, there is uncertainty of model's performance degradation after conversion. This study evaluates three prominent OCR models-PaddleOCR (CNN-RNN architecture), UltOCR (MASTER architecture), and TrOCR (Transformer-based architecture)-selected for their distinct architectures. Baseline, TFLite 32-bit, and quantized 16-bit versions of these models were tested on datasets containing words, numbers, and sentences to identify which architecture maintains the performance after conversion. The findings indicate that PaddleOCR and UltOCR achieved minimal degradation. However, TrOCR experienced a significant accuracy loss of 6.81% post-conversion in the sentences category. The study provides valuable insights in selecting which OCR architecture should be used for edge deployment.

articleTitle: Robust Sliding Mode Control of a Quadrotor With Disturbance Rejection for Enhanced Stability and Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This research presents a comprehensive analysis of quadrotor stabilization and trajectory tracking control using Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) with integrated disturbance rejection. The nonlinear dynamics of the quadrotor are formulated using the Newton-Euler approach, accounting for six degrees of freedom. The PID controller is implemented as a baseline, while the SMC is designed for enhanced robustness to model uncertainties and external perturbations, with a disturbance observer for managing time-varying disturbances. A rigorous Lyapunov stability proof ensures global asymptotic stability of the SMC-controlled system. Extensive simulations evaluate both controllers in terms of tracking accuracy, control effort, and robustness to external disturbances. Results show that SMC outperforms PID in dis-turbance rejection, tracking accuracy, and robustness, making it ideal for UAV applications in complex environments.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Three Fingered Under Actuated Prosthetic Hand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: The study presented a mechanical design of a three fingered under-actuated prosthetic hand. As multi-fingered prosthetic hands are currently being researched and developed globally, the work began with an examination of the prosthetic hand with less fingers and actuators to reduce weight and cost and to increase adaptively. It has been observed that only three fingers out of the five can cover most of the basic tasks of the usual routine. Whereas actuators for each link make it heavy and complex so under actuation phenomenon is used to get phalanx control where less actuators are used than degree pf freedom. Therefore, this study focuses upon an innovative approach to develop a three fingered prosthetic hand by utilizing under-actuation in order to nullify the complexity and to get a much cheaper solution.

articleTitle: Improving Road Safety With Enhanced Vehicle Detection for Night-time Traffic in Mirpur
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This paper presents a study on improving night-time vehicle detection in the Mirpur region through a modified neural network model. Given the challenges of low visibility at night, the research focused on optimizing a deep learning algorithm to enhance detection accuracy. A dataset of 10,000 images covering various vehicle types was collected and annotated to train and test the model. The study found a 7% increase in detection performance compared to the standard model, highlighting the potential for tailored algorithms in specific environmental conditions. The findings suggest significant implications for road safety and autonomous driving systems, particularly in regions with similar night-time driving challenges. The research contributes to the broader field of computer vision by showing the effectiveness of model optimization in real-world conditions.

articleTitle: Design & Implementation of a Healthcare Kiosk: An Effective Way to Collect Patient Vitals for Better Management of Non-Communicable Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Health monitoring systems have become essential in modern healthcare by enabling continuous observation of vital signs through wearable and home-based monitoring devices. However, better management of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) requires multiple such devices integrated into a comprehensive, easy-to-use, and do at-home kiosk/station where the patients can log their vitals themselves. The NCD management requires sensors for blood pressure, glucose levels, oxygen saturation, cardiac activity, and temperature. Therefore, these key sensory devices have been integrated into kiosk, including sensor-based automatic blood pressure monitor, OCR-based blood glucose monitor, pulse oximeter, electrocardiograph sensor, and temperature sensor. Complete details of the mechatronic system have been provided in the manuscript. Each episode of vitals collection is logged to create a personal chronicle for both the patients and the doctors to analyze vis-a-vis the prescribed medicine, diet, and exercise-based management paradigms. Enhancements in accessibility and efficiency have been achieved through integration with telemedicine and AI, enabling remote monitoring and timely medical interventions. This system allows the patients to manage their health without frequent hospital visits, improving patient outcomes and promoting sustainable healthcare.

articleTitle: Design and Control of 2DoF Wearable Robot Arm for Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Robotic therapy is gaining more popularity because of its proven success in regaining upper extremity movements and loco-motor skills, especially in stroke patients. In this work, the development of a low cost 2 degrees of freedoms (DoF) wearable robot arm is presented. This robotic exoskeleton device is aimed at rehabilitation of upper extremity disabilities caused by stroke or other brain ailments. The robot arm allows for flexion-extension movements at the shoulder and elbow joints to assist in targeted therapy of these important upper limb articulations. Notably, the device boasts several design enhancements over its low cost predecessors. Problems with bulky design and power losses due to its own inertia, in particular, have been effectively addressed, resulting in a more streamlined and efficient system. In addition to design and manufacture, Sliding mode based Cartesian compliance control simulation of the devices and a real-time joint space PID control results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) with Spherical Wheels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: An unmanned ground vehicle is a mobile robot that moves around without any human, and it is generally remote operated. Its quality of being lightweight and compact makes it highly desirable to be used in missions that involve high levels of risk and danger like surveillance, inspection, reconnaissance. Typical UGVs that consist of two- or four-wheels experience limitations in the maneuverability of the robot. This research is aimed to design and develop a prototype of UGV which is omni-directional. Spherical wheels, introduced as new type of omni-wheels were designed, 3D printed, and the rest of the body was manufactured keeping in mind to keep the robot as lightweight as possible. The wheels had an active rotational component as well as a passive one. Complete calculations and analysis of the wheels were done using ANSYS. A comprehensive outlook on the mobility controls of the UGV was explored and the research concluded with suggestions of materials that could be used for the manufacturing of wheels on an industrial scale to make the UGV robust and able to withstand impacts.

articleTitle: Enhancing Thrust in Flapping Airfoils Through Wake Interactions with Oscillating Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Inspired by the natural motion of insects, fish, and other animals, flapping airfoils have gained significant importance due to their applications in fields such as ship propulsion, micro aerial vehicles, and autonomous underwater vehicles. Over the past two decades, extensive research has focused on understanding the dynamics of these airfoils, their thrust production capabilities, and methods to enhance this thrust in unsteady flows. This study investigates how the presence of a cylinder oscillating due to incoming flow affects the thrust performance of the flapping airfoil. The results indicate that the flapping airfoil generates increased thrust when placed in the wake of the oscillating cylinder compared to a scenario without the cylinder's wake. A direct relationship has been found between the strouhal number (St) of the flapping airfoil and its pitching amplitude, which significantly influences the airfoil's performance. This analysis highlights the potential for optimizing flapping airfoil efficiency through strategic selection of flapping parameters and the placement of an oscillating cylinder.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Autonomous Robotic Grasping and Sorting System for Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a deep learning (DL)-based vision system for real-time object detection, grasping, and sorting using a UR5e robotic manipulator, aimed to address the challenges faced in industrial automation while grasping and sorting randomly placed objects in the workspace. The system utilizes a fine-tuned detection model, YOLOv8s, trained on a custom dataset of three distinct objects for testing a real-time grasping and sorting system using DL. Once the objects are detected in the workspace, image processing techniques are applied to each detected object to extract the accurate grasping information like the centroid and the orientation. This information is then converted to the robotic arm-based coordinate system to ensure the accurate manipulation of the objects in the workspace. The system is tested in the cluttered environment of the tabletop workspace to grasp and sort the objects, significantly enhancing both speed and accuracy in real-time industrial tasks. Experimental results show grasping accuracy of 93.33%, demonstrating the system's potential to improve automation efficiency in Industry 4.0 applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wind Speed Estimation with Least Squares Generative Adversarial Networks: A Case Study of Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Wind energy has emerged as a key player in sustainable power generation. Accurate prediction of wind speed is critical for optimizing wind farm operations, energy output forecasting, and reducing dependency on traditional power sources. In this study, we propose a Least-Squares Generative Adversarial Network (LSGAN) for wind speed prediction in a specific region of Pakistan, utilizing data from Tandoghulamali, which includes features like wind speeds at various altitudes and wind direction. The model is designed to predict wind speed at 80 meters, a crucial target variable for wind turbine operations. The LSGAN model effectively leverages adversarial training, achieving high accuracy with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.54 and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.77. Through a detailed comparison of actual versus predicted values, the model demonstrates its ability to generalize well across unseen data, with stable performance during the adversarial learning process. This approach opens up new possibilities for applying advanced machine learning techniques in renewable energy forecasting, particularly in regions with sparse historical data.

articleTitle: A Lightweight CNN for RGB-D Grasp Classification in Computer Vision-Based Prosthetic Hands
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Prosthetic hand development has progressed significantly from basic mechanical designs to advanced systems that incorporate computer vision for enhanced functionality. However, the challenge now is creating a lightweight, accurate and computationally efficient model suitable for integrating embedded microcontrollers in prosthetic devices. This paper presents a novel framework based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with just 160,000 trainable parameters and a size of under 1MB, making it viable for deployment in microcontrollers like Arduino, ESP, and Raspberry Pi. The framework has a comprehensive input of 32x32x3 which incorporates grey-scaled RGB, depth, and masked data. The presented model is tested on a newly structured RGB-D dataset containing 51 objects across 7 grasp types, achieving 99% accuracy with minimal computational resources.

articleTitle: Robust State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using a Nonlinearity-Aware PID Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: An accurate estimation of state of charge (SOC) is crucial for the safe and reliable operation of Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the complex and intermittent nature of LIBs against dynamic operating conditions makes this task highly challenging. Therefore, a novel nonlinearity-aware PID observer is proposed to ensure enhanced robustness and improved accuracy in dynamic scenarios. The proposed observer is designed using a second-order equivalent circuit model (ECM) whose observability is rigorously discussed. A strategy to detect nonlinearity is integrated with the proposed design to adapt to the most suitable mechanism in highly dynamic situations. An experimental testbench, using an INR21700 cell whose parameters are identified experimentally, is constructed to verify the practicability of the proposed design. Furthermore, comparative results against highly dynamic loadfiles underscore improved accuracy, enhanced robustness, and faster convergence, demonstrating the proposed design's effectiveness in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: An accurate estimation of battery state of charge (SOC) is crucial to ensure the safety of Li-ion batteries (LIBs), and the recent boom in machine learning (ML) has illustrated a strong potential for SOC estimation. However, the ignorance of LIB internal dynamics greatly limits the performance of ML-based methods. Therefore, this work incorporates multiple battery internal dynamics into the ML-based method to ensure enhanced performance. First, using a simple mechanism based on the LIB model, the open circuit voltage, ohmic response, and temperature-corrected pattern are extracted from the measured data and provided as inputs to the neural networks (NNs). Then, to ensure time adaptability and accuracy, the predictions of the proposed design are adjusted using short-term Ampere-hour results. The proposed technique is validated using different real-world driving profiles. The comparative results with benchmark NNs-based methods verify a >60% reduction in root mean square error, demonstrating the effectiveness of incorporating battery internal dynamics into NNs.

articleTitle: Optimization of Microbial Fuel Cells: Enhancing Electrical Output Through Gradient-Based Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Microbial Fuel Cells (MFCs) are environment-friendly devices to generate energy through microbial metabolism of the chemical energy of organic compounds. Few of the critical challenges of implementing MFCs are their low power density, high internal resistance, and poor electron transport. These factors are major drawbacks to the MFCs efficiency and ability to scale up MFCs. The proposed work aims to enhance the MFC performance by optimizing the proportions of key operational parameters to overcome the implementation challenges. These parameters include Substrate Concentration <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S)$</tex>, Anodophilic Biomass <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(x_{a})$</tex>, Methanogenic Biomass <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(x_{m})$</tex>, and Oxidized Mediator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M_{ox})$</tex>. The parameters are optimized using a Gradient Based Optimization (GBO). During the optimization process, it was imperative to establish a sound mathematical model that predicted MFC's biological and physical behavior. With the implementation of the GBO algorithm, the output current is enhanced by 8. 89 percent. The results shows that promising future of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Velodyne LiDAR-Guided Safe Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Navigation Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: A goal of safe reinforcement learning is to minimize reward while respecting safety constraints, but achieving that balance remains a challenge. Popular approaches often lead to overly cautious policies that produce suboptimal results in different environments. This paper explores the potential of dual-delay deterministic policy gradients and proximal policy optimization combined with Velodyne VLP-16 LIDAR data to process the data in specific autonomous environment. The surroundings are searched for points of interest (POI) for potential navigation directions, and an ideal waypoint is chosen depending on the data at hand. We deliver comprehensions into improving the performance of Safe RL by enhance perception of receiving data with LiDAR, allowing us to analyze its ability to navigate in dynamic environments while maintaining safety and efficiency using safe reinforcement learning algorithms

articleTitle: Automated Hematological Analysis:Advances in Segmentation Approaches and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Hematological analysis is crucial for diagnosing blood disorders such as leukemia and anemia, a process that has traditionally depended on manual microscopy, and is susceptible to variability and human error. The quest for more reliable and efficient diagnostic methods has led to the development of automated systems. This review examines the methods used for automated blood cell segmentation, with a particular emphasis on deep learning approaches such as semantic and instance segmentation. Advanced models like Mask R-CNN and DeepLabv3+ were evaluated for their effectiveness in accurately segmenting and identifying blood components in complex histological images. The findings revealed that Mask R-CNN achieved a segmentation accuracy of 92%, while DeepLabv3+ came in close behind at 94.5%. Both models significantly surpassed traditional methods, which generally provide accuracy rates of 75–80 %. Despite these advancements, the review highlights ongoing challenges related to the robustness and scalability of these techniques in clinical settings. The paper concludes by emphasizing the transformative potential of deep learning in hematological diagnostics and calls for further research to address current limitations and improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Advancement in Smart Cane Technology: Enhancing Mobility for the Visually Impaired Using ROS and LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Visual impairment affects the ability to navigate independently in an unknown environment due to reliance on human/dog assistance, potential miscommunication, and discomfort during mobility. To make the visually impaired (VI) individuals self-reliant and confident in their mobility the proposed system has been developed that contains a light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensor for obstacle detection and two omni-wheels coupled with the DC gear encoder motors for precise movement in any direction without lifting the cane. Hector Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), A *, and steering wheel algorithms have been implemented in the robot operating system (ROS) for real-time environment mapping, efficient path planning, and navigating in an unknown indoor static environment, respectively. The Raspberry Pi 3B+ and Arduino Mega 2560 are used in the master-slave configuration for decision-making on path planning and controlling the maneuverability of the system in real-time. The proposed system in the paper is successfully tested on one subject in two indoor environments. The results demonstrate that the system serves as an assistive mobile robot, helping the VI individual to navigate confidently in an unknown environment and reach the destination without assistance.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning With Multi-Head Attention for Accurate Extraction of Medicine From Handwritten Prescriptions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Extracting medication names from handwritten doctor prescriptions is challenging due to the wide variability in handwriting styles and prescription formats. This paper presents a robust method for extracting medicine names using a combination of Mask R-CNN and Transformer-based Optical Character Recognition (TrOCR) with Multi-Head Attention and Positional Embeddings. A novel dataset, featuring diverse handwritten prescriptions from various regions of Pakistan, was utilized to fine-tune the model on different handwriting styles. The Mask R-CNN model segments the prescription images to focus on the medicinal sections, while the TrOCR model, enhanced by Multi-Head Attention and Positional Embeddings, transcribes the isolated text. The transcribed text is then matched against a pre-existing database for accurate identification. The proposed approach achieved a character error rate (CER) of 1.4% on standard benchmarks, highlighting its potential as a reliable and efficient tool for automating medicine name extraction.

articleTitle: Analysis of Motor Imagery-Based fNIRS-BCI for Knee Flexion and Extension
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This study aimed to explore the potential of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) as a non-invasive technique for detecting hemodynamic responses in cortical brain activities during motor imagery (MI) tasks. Specifically, the study focused on classifying multiclass MI tasks with fNIRS data. A total of 10 healthy individuals participated in the experiment, where they were instructed to perform motor imagery tasks. A multi-channel continuous wave fNIRS system records the signals from the motor cortex for knee flexion and extension imagery tasks. Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), comparatively computationally efficient, algorithms were used to classify the data for fNIRS-based BCI applications. The SVM classifier performed comparatively better than the LDA classifier in accuracy, with 88.8% and 89.4% for two-feature and three-feature combinations. Brain activation maps show the increased activation for flexion movement of the knee. Future research should focus on refining the classification process through feature selection, preprocessing improvements, and ensemble methods to enhance accuracy.

articleTitle: Internet of Robots: An Open-source Framework for Cloud-Based Global Remote Control and Monitoring of Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: With the growing prevalence of service robots across various sectors, there is a growing need to ensure seamless connectivity between robots and users from virtually anywhere in the world. This demand has driven extensive research over the past decade, leading to the emergence of innovative technologies such as the Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT) and Cloud Robotics. While various studies have proposed solutions to achieve global connectivity between robots and end-users, most existing approaches are tailored to specific robots, such as drones, or are designed for niche applications. Moreover, these solutions are often not open-source and limited in terms of scope, adaptability, scalability, and general usability. This research presents a comprehensive, practical approach for implementation of IoRT and cloud robotics which utilizes a three-level client-server architecture that includes a cloud server layer, robot client layer, and user client layer. Utilizing Django for application development hosted on AWS Cloud, the implementation demonstrates the potential of cloud robotics to provide real-time, bidirectional communication between robots and users over an infinite communication range.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Based Brake Failure Detection & Collision Avoidance Model for Automated Driving System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: The manual and automated braking system is intended to prevent rear-end collisions. However, unforeseen malfunctions within the vehicle's system during braking could potentially cause accidents. Collision Warning (CW) systems are safety technologies in vehicles that aid drivers in preventing collisions. This paper introduces a fuzzy-assisted pre-warning system for brake testing that considers multiple factors contributing to brake failure, along with a post-failure CW algorithm tailored for heavy commercial vehicles. Simulations conducted using NetLogo demonstrate that accidents can be prevented during brake failure through appropriate adjustments in vehicle speed. The proposed collision avoidance system has been validated for its effectiveness, and the results are encouraging and enhance road user safety.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Energy Prediction of Hybrid Solar-Wind Energy Harvesters Using MPPT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: The ever-growing demand for reliable and sustainable energy solutions has shifted the trend from standalone power systems towards higher efficient Hybrid Solar-Wind Power Systems. This paper presents a comparative analysis of a machine learning based energy prediction for a hybrid solar-wind energy harvester using MPPT. The solar-wind hybrid systems interfaced with MPPT can simultaneously capture both solar and wind power, and machine learning algorithms are involved for optimized multi-mode operation across different environmental conditions. The models used including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest Regression (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to analyze the performance of hybrid energy harvester. This type of energy combination is beneficial for coastal areas and optimal solution for sustainable energy production from renewable sources.

articleTitle: Autonomous Detection and Geolocalization of Targets Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles for Search and Rescue (SAR) Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have demon-strated remarkable potential in remote sensing and land sur-veying, making them indispensable in Search and Rescue (SAR) missions worldwide. Numerous incidents have reported the use of drones to search for targets such as missing persons or stranded vehicles. Traditionally, these missions involve manually controlled drones with live video transmission systems, requiring rescue per-sonnel to identify and locate targets manually. Other approaches involve the use of photogrammetry, which is computationally expensive and requires significant amount of time before yielding results. These approaches can be cumbersome and inefficient in time-critical situations. This research proposes a solution utilizing low-cost drones capable of autonomously surveying areas to search for lost targets, such as missing persons or vehicles, and acquiring their geographical coordinates which are then mapped using a Graphical User Interface (GUI) both in real-time and offline. The proposed autonomous system aims to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of UAVs in SAR operations, providing rapid and accurate situational awareness, thereby improving response times and mission success rates.

articleTitle: A Parametric and Generative Based Panels Design Optimization for Mass Timber Panel Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: With the development of Construction 4.0 and digital technologies, off-site construction has evolved and become a practical choice for rapid construction. In today's fast-paced manufacturing framework, there is a need to automate every construction step, especially the design and analysis phases of mass timber panel manufacturing, as these two steps are highly expert's dependent. This study summarizes a case to design multiple variants of mass timber panels using parametric and generative modeling. Integrating these technologies helps create speedy and tailored design solutions in the automation setting. A building information modeling (BIM) based on a 3D parametric design of a timber panel is generated, followed by optimizations via generative design. Focusing on the Canadian construction industry, different types of mass timber are examined to analyze and optimize design features such as stud width, stud bays, and weight-bearing capacity. This study aims to support customization and adaptability at the yield of less time and effort for ongoing industrial automation.

articleTitle: AI-Based Early Detection of Coronary Artery Disease Using Atherosclerosis Inflammatory and MicroRNA Biomarkers in Angina Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is one of the most common causes of sudden cardiac arrest and is responsible for a high percentage of global mortality. Early diagnosis of CAD in patients with chest pain is challenging. Coronary angiography, an invasive procedure that is not widely available in developing countries, confirms the diagnosis of CAD. It is imperative to establish noninvasive biomarkers for the early diagnosis of CAD in patients with angina. Motivated by two recent medical diagnostic studies that used novel molecular (microRNA) and chemical (atherosclerosis-inflammatory) biomarkers for early detection of CAD, the proposed study explores the hidden potential of novel biomarkers using machine learning (ML). The study combines the biomarkers of two medical studies and presents a NUMS-NIHD dataset. From the complete dataset, the best feature set is shortlisted after an extensive evaluative search in the biomarker feature space. Ten ML classifiers are applied to the selected biomarker inputs, including clinical, chemical, and molecular cardiac biomarkers. To select optimal biomarker-classifier combinations, experiments use K-fold cross-validation. The results of K-fold cross-validation are validated against a hold-out set of data. The results are then compared to current state-of-the-art benchmark studies. The detection strategy achieved an accuracy of 90.18%, a sensitivity of 92.33 % and a specificity of 100.00%. The proposed study validated previous medical diagnostic studies and significantly improved the results. These ML biomarkers-classifier combinations can be used to exclude healthy individuals non-invasively before angiography.

articleTitle: Compensating Force Imbalance Using Anchored Beam Coupling Mechanism in MEMS Tuning Fork Gyroscope (TFG) Drive Frame Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This paper presents an improved tuning fork gyroscope (TFG) structure utilizing two gyroscope drive resonator frames and a diamond-shaped coupling spring mechanism. It explores a two-degree-of-freedom system for the drive mode frame with a coupling mechanism to reduce external vibration sensitivity while keeping angular rate sensitivity. Expressions are derived to study and optimize the coupling spring structure. FEM modeling using ANSYS software validates the expressions that are derived. Simulations were performed to ensure anti-phase motion and avoid structural imbalance induced in-phase motion. Simulations demonstrate compensation for force imbalance and preservation of anti-phase motion. FEM modal analysis confirms a significant frequency separation of 10.90 kHz between in-phase and anti-phase resonant frequencies, with values at 6.81 kHz and 17.713 kHz, respectively. The improved frequency separation in TFG can ensure robustness against external environmental vibrations when fabrication imperfections occur and ensure better reliability for the measurement of angular velocity in inertial sensing applications.

articleTitle: Time Series Forecasting of KSE-100 Index Using a Hybrid ESN-LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: The volatility and complexity of stock markets, particularly in emerging economies like Pakistan, pose significant challenges for accurate forecasting. This paper aims to improve the predictive accuracy of the Karachi Stock Exchange index (KSE-100) by comparing and combining advanced deep learning models. The research investigates the effectiveness of Echo State Networks (ESN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and a hybrid ESN-LSTM model in capturing both short-term fluctuations and long-term trends. Daily KSE-100 index prices from September 1, 2019, to September 1, 2024, were used, with scaled closing price, 50- and 200-day moving averages as input features. The models' performances were evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), R-squared and Directional Accuracy (DA). Results indicate that the ESN-LSTM hybrid model outperformed both individual ESN and LSTM models, achieving the lowest MAE of 513.10 and RMSE of 650.59, along with the highest R-squared of 0.975 and DA of 94.12%. The superior performance of the hybrid model is attributed to its ability to use the efficient temporal feature extraction of ESNs and the long-term memory capabilities of LSTMs. These findings suggest that hybrid approaches can significantly improve stock market forecasting accuracy in emerging markets. Future research should explore the integration of sentiment analysis and macroeconomic indicators to further enhance predictive capabilities.

articleTitle: Enhanced Military Aircraft Detection Using YOLOv5s with Hyperparameter Evolution in Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Aircraft detection in aerial imaging plays an important role in various applications, such as surveillance, reconnaissance, and disaster response. Unmanned aerial vehicles and satellite imagery are valuable resources for remote sensing applications. The detection of aircraft in these images is challenging because of the diverse aircraft types, varying image scales, and complex backgrounds. In this study, a modified YOLOv5s that incorporates the Adam optimizer instead of standard Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is proposed. Furthermore, the impact of genetic evolution on both the base and optimized models was studied. The best hyperparameters obtained after 100 generations were used to train YOLOv5s. Optimizing hyperparameters through genetic evolution and switching the optimizer from SGD to Adam increased the mAP score from the base YOLOv5s model. A mean average precision of 96.57% was achieved for the Adam optimizer, which outperformed the base YOLOv5s model by a margin of 1.8%. The proposed method outperformed YOLOv5m and had a similar mAP score to YOLOv51, making it a feasible option for applications that require high accuracy, low computational cost, and fast inference times. Genetic evolution increased the mAP score of the model using the SGD optimizer but did not improve the results of the model using the Adam optimizer.

articleTitle: Trash Detection in Water Bodies Using Yolo With Explainable AI Insight
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Waste disposal into water bodies is a serious concern for environmental engineers, often resulting in urban flooding, soil degradation in agricultural areas, and freshwater pollution. Additionally, trash accumulation in water bodies threatens ma-rine life by introducing contaminants through storm drains, rivers, and other channels. Furthermore, the unique character-istics of underwater environments, including high noise levels, low visibility, and color variation, pose challenges for trash detection. Thus, addressing this issue is crucial for environmental sustainability. The work focuses on both floating and submerged trash in water bodies. Typically, the detection of trash on water bodies is impacted by environmental variability, diverse appearance, and background clutter. These conditions also make usual object detection techniques less effective. Deep learning methods have shown promise in handling challenging visual tasks, therefore researchers have turned to them to get over these challenges. In this work, we focus on applying different versions of YOLO to the problem of water trash detection. To assess these models' performance, we use four different datasets: Trash Flow rate Dataset, DeepTrash, FloW, and TrashICRA. Each dataset represents various trash types under different conditions such as underwater trash and floating trash. Our study attempts to identify the best method suitable for the detection of aquatic waste. Our results highlight the effectiveness of YOLO variants in identifying the presence of trash in water ecosystems. By leveraging Grad-CAM we gain insights into the interpretability and transparency of deep learning models thus enabling Explainable AI. This approach will also contribute to the understanding and trustworthiness of artificial systems deployed for trash detection applications by providing a transparent view of decision making process of deep learning models.

articleTitle: ML Based Light-Weight Security Protocol for IoFT Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Forest plays a vital role in environmental change and the protection of forests is the utmost important thing. The study attempts to suggest a solution for a smart forest (Internet of Forest Things). As nowadays, the Internet of Things is emerging very vastly and a large number of researchers are working towards the field of Internet of Forest Things (loFT). The protection of smart forests is of utmost importance because the infrastructure is physically unprotected and they generate huge data about the forest. Due to scalability, smart forest controllers are small-sized and low-cost devices with less computational capabilities. Keeping it in mind, the designed algorithms should be lightweight so that they can meet the requirements. To address this issue, this paper proposes a machine learning approach to develop a lightweight security solution to address data altering and man-in-the-middle attacks. The algorithm generates a link fingerprint of the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) value of the communicating IoFT node. The packet is sent to the server unit and it is decoded and matched with the table to identify the path. A trained machine learning model at the server gets the RSSI value from the packet and successfully classify about the presence of an attack.

articleTitle: A Cryptography-Based Framework for Securing Medical Imaging Data in Robotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Medical imaging data is crucial in robotics-assisted diagnostics and interventions, particularly in neurology. Ensuring the security and privacy of this sensitive data is increasingly challenging in the context of robotic systems. This study presents a robust framework to secure MRI brain images using the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm, tailored for use in robotics applications. The AES algorithm is chosen for its high level of data confidentiality and integrity, making it well-suited for protecting sensitive medical information in robotic systems. Encrypted MRI images are decrypted and then processed by a convolutional neural network (CNN), specifically AlexNet, integrated into the robotic platform to classify the images as either tumorous or healthy. The classification performance is thoroughly evaluated using confusion matrices and performance plots, assessing the accuracy of the system. The project is implemented using Python, and the results demonstrate significant improvements over recent advancements in this field. This study not only enhances the security of medical imaging data within robotics applications but also contributes to improving the precision and reliability of robotic diagnostic systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of MEMS Tuning Fork Gyroscope Designs with Microlever Amplification Mechanism for Enhanced Sensitivity and Robustness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of two MEMS Tuning Fork Gyroscope (TFG) designs employing microlever amplification mechanisms for sensitivity amplification in the sense mode. An input frame added in microlever amplification frame to increase the robustness of MEMS gyroscope. Design A incorporates a non-anchored input frame in microlever, while Design B features an anchored input frame in microlever. Frequency response analysis and modal analysis were performed using CoventorMEMS+ to evaluate the impact of input frame of microlever on undesired mode suppression, mechanical sensitivity, and robustness. The results indicate that anchoring the microlever in Design B significantly reduces quadrature displacement arise because of environmental linear acceleration in the sense mode while maintaining comparable amplified sensitivity to Design A. Design B offers enhanced stability and robustness, making it a more suitable candidate for precision applications such as autonomous vehicle navigation systems.

articleTitle: A Multi-Sensor Approach for Thermal Environment Monitoring in Public Transport
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Globally it is found that many vehicles do not have built-in intelligent monitoring systems which is very much dangerous especially when the temperature of the indoor environment is rising. This research fulfills the need by designing a thermal indoor environment monitoring device that increases the safety and intelligence of vehicles. The device collects and records a number of environmentally significant parameters like temperature, pressure, both indoor and outdoor humidity, light intensity, TVOC, CO2 levels, and GPS position. Large amounts of data were collected from different cars, buses and trains for both local city and inter-city environments. These datasets helped in the deployment of intelligent monitoring and management techniques which helped with the intervention. The outcomes of our experiments show that it is possible to enhance the safety and comfort of car passengers with the help of innovative solutions, for instance, pre-staging air conditioning when the temperature starts to rise. This research benefits the smart vehicle development field and provides a strong solution to Pakistan's environmental monitoring issues in the transportation industry.

articleTitle: Kinematic and Dynamic Analysis of All-Terrain Wheeled Robot: Modeling and Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This study presents the kinematic and dynamic analysis of a six-wheeled all-terrain robot designed for challenging environments such as rough terrains and slopes. Differentially controlled wheels and shock absorbers are also used in the robot's construction to give it high mobility and stability on the four surfaces. The first part of the project aimed at developing a SolidWorks 3D model of the robot, while the first element of design concentrated on engineering such structural parts of the robot as the chassis, the wheels, and the suspension system. After the design phase, the authors used simulations on ANSYS to perform kinematic and dynamic analyses and study the robot's operations under various conditions. These simulations checked the robot's stability, wheel traction, torque distribution, and the forces received by the robot during the movement, proving its ability to manage obstacles and travel through rough terrains. Moreover, measurements were made through calculations, which showed other essential factors like torque, the forces acting between the wheel and the terrain, energy consumption, and the load distributed over the wheels. The results from this study show the robot's capability to be used in disaster response, environment mapping, and surveillance in rugged areas. Besides the beneficial ability of simulations to reveal the details of the robot's operations on different terrains, the analytical results provide an excellent starting point for forthcoming design modifications in multi-terrain robots, with possible further improvements in adaptability and energy usage.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Weed Detection for Precision Agriculture Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Weed detection and management is an intricate and formidable challenge, affecting the efficiency of human agricultural practices. Object detection has merged as a key technique in precision-based agriculture for combatting this issue. This paper analyzes the performance of two cutting-edge object detection models namely YOLOv8x and Faster RCNN on a specialized weed-detection dataset. By leveraging transfer learning, these models proved computationally feasible and accurate. The models were built and trained in a Kaggle environment, promoting a more collaborative approach to developing and implementing deep-learning models. The Faster RCNN model showcased a comparatively better mAP as compared to the YOLOv8x model. This paper highlights the significance of advanced models like Faster RCNN and YOLOv8x for precision agriculture while advocating for further research in deep-learning techniques for promoting resource-efficient agricultural and farming practices.

articleTitle: TezNet: An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network for Optical Coherence Tomography Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Retinal diseases such as Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV), Drusen, and Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) can severely impair vision and are challenging to reverse if detected late. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) serves as a non-invasive imaging modality to diagnose these conditions through cross-sectional retinal images. Current advancements in retinal disease detection predominantly focus on fine-tuning larger models to achieve high accuracy, often at the expense of substantial training time and data requirements. We introduce an innovative Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) named TezNet that is deeper and wider than existing custom CNNs for the dataset used in this research yet maintains a lightweight architecture with only 3.6 million parameters. This high efficiency is accomplished by leveraging depthwise and spatial separable convolutional techniques without employing preprocessing techniques or noise reduction filters. The data augmentation techniques generate diverse image qualities, ensuring robust predictions across various scenarios. By training exclusively on a single dataset, our model achieves rapid training times and optimal resource utilization, minimizing the risk of overfitting. This blend of advanced parameter optimization, minimal preprocessing, and strategic data augmentation underscores the potential of our CNN model for swift, precise, and resource-efficient retinal disease detection. TezNet model achieves a remarkable 96% accuracy, competing closely with state-of-the-art networks like ResNet50 (over 23M parameters), InceptionV3 (over 25M parameters), and ResNeXt (89M parameters).

articleTitle: Slam Based Robot Find Target EV to Plugin in Complex Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging in complex environments presents significant challenges, precise and adaptable interaction between robotic systems and vehicle charging plugs. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) integrated with a robotic arm to facilitate autonomous charging. Methodology used SLAM techniques to enable the robot to accurately perceive and navigate dynamic and cluttered environments. The robotic arm, equipped with sensors and actuators, is guided by this precise environmental mapping to engage charging ports on a diverse range of vehicle models without human intervention. Implementation of the robotic system, including the integration of a vision-based kick algorithm that ensures robustness and adaptability in real-time obstacle detection and navigation. 3D simulations scenarios and robot to vehicle(R2V), robot 2 robot(R2R),robot to everything(R2X) communication demonstrating significant improvements in operational efficiency and adaptability compared to traditional charging solutions. Robot, IOT and EV charging applications increase autonomy and efficiency in electric vehicle infrastructure, high level of safety, economically benefits and monitoring techniques.

articleTitle: Bare Printed Circuit Board Defects Localization and Detection Using YOLOv5 Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: A printed circuit board (PCB) is a vital component of any electronic device. Over the years, the need to manufacture PCBs in large volumes has become a necessity due to technological advancement and the expansion of the consumer market. Small defects in the PCB signal trace can have adverse consequences on the functionality of an electronic device. Initially, the quality control process of PCB inspection was carried out manually which was not only tedious but also susceptible to human error. To automate this process, different techniques were developed using classical machine vision that comprised reference comparison, subtraction of images and morphological operations. The methods were effective and reduced inspection time but were sensitive to noise, rotation, and scaling of images. It was difficult to detect defects in complex patterns and only a small fraction of defects could be detected through classical techniques. In this study, four YOLOv5 models were tested for the classification and localization of defects in PCBs. Transfer learning on the bare PCB defect dataset was implemented using pretrained weights of YOLOv5. The PCB dataset was composed of 2,079 images with 6 classes of PCB defects. Data augmentations were carried out to increase the dataset which enhanced performance and generalizability of the models. The models were trained and tested at different image resolutions. Promising experimental results were achieved with the medium YOLOv5 model reaching a mean average precision of 96.92%.

articleTitle: A Soft Robotics Approach to Prosthetic Hands: Integrating 3D Printing Techniques and Embedded Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: The development of soft robotics hand has progressed significantly, evolving from a pneumatically actuated solution for industrial applications to a lightweight and easy-to-manufacture solution for 3d printed prosthetic hands. However, existing soft prosthetic hands often lack anthropomorphic appearances, intrinsic structural integrity, and sufficient feedback to the amputees, leading to a high rate of abandonment of prosthetic hands. This paper presents a design of a 3d printed soft robotic hand based on a monolithic design with an embedded camera and anthropomorphic appearance. The hand is fabricated using the flexible 3d printable material TPU-95 with an embedded Raspberry Pie Cam module for increased functionality. The hand utilizes a cable-driven mechanism integrated with five rotary actuators capable of multiple grasp patterns. Our design weighs around 246 grams with all the electronic components embedded inside the hand. This paper discusses the mechanical design, 3d printing methodology for the fabrication of the fingers, actuation mechanisms, and the results of the soft prosthetic hand's performance.

articleTitle: Human-Centered Design and Development of an Elderly Care Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Constituting to the demographic age shift in many regions of the world, technological advancement in the care sector, to deliver quality services to the elders, is now in more demand than ever. One such advancement is the evolution of socially assistive and care robots that promise sustainable, reliable, and safe human-robot interaction to meet geriatric needs. This paper presents the design and development of Silver Companion: a geriatric care robot for the elderly. The target audience chosen for the research phase is the socially isolated elderly community of East Asia and Central Europe which make up about 45% of their total elderly population. Considering the human-centered design paradigm, the technical and psychological aspects of the robot have been devised. The form and functions of the robot have been based on the product design principles. The whole development journey has been subjected to the identified elderly needs and the robot has been tested under multiple use-case scenarios, ideated for possibly fulfilling those needs. The robot has been equipped with assistive and interactive features like voice interaction, complementing micro-gestures and robot expressions, seamless navigation, and robot perception enhanced by a tilt-pan mechanism, all contributing towards making the robot capable of uplifting the well-being and quality of life of seniors.

articleTitle: Pushing and Rotating a Heavy Mass Rigid Body Using an Omnidirectional Aerial Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This paper presents the pushing and rotation of a heavy rigid body using an omnidirectional actively tilted aerial manipulator, controlled via a hybrid force/position controller. Unlike conventional unmanned aerial vehicles, the proposed system enables precise horizontal force application, making it ideal for aerial physical interaction tasks. The hybrid controller is implemented in the Robot Operating System and validated through extensive simulations in a Gazebo physics-engine-based environment. The manipulator's performance was evaluated in two scenarios: circular trajectory tracking and the rotation of a heavy rigid mass. Results demonstrated its capability to follow complex trajectories with high accuracy and exert sustained forces for object manipulation. The system exhibited excellent stability and precision, underscoring its potential for real-world applications in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Assistive Feeding System: Design and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Old people and patients with limited or complete motor impairment had always face difficulty in their daily life task in which most important and frequent is eating meals, such people need assistant like nurse to feed them. In this paper we worked on an assistive feeding system based on 6 Degree of Freedom fixed base open-source robotic arm with active assistance. The manipulator is 3D printed by fused deposition modelling technique using PLA + material and a counterweight mechanism is introduced to reduce the motor torque requirements hence reducing the power consumption of the system. The system is divided into 2 sub-systems which are hybrid-vision system to get location of mouth of the person to feed and, scooping and delivery system which uses manipulator and control system to feed the food. The system is completely embedded on raspberry pi with wireless access for user and programmer. Finally, we discuss the results of our system and limitations in the methodologies used.

articleTitle: Keypoints Estimation on Partial Point Clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Estimating 3D keypoints of an object has achieved considerable interest, especially in computer graphics and ma-chine vision. The complexity of the problem increases when the object is noisy, decimated, or partially occluded. To this end, we present an approach to estimate 3D keypoints from the partial PCDs such that they also highlight the object's missing parts. It is based on two modules: shape completion and keypoints estimation. The first module computes the object's missing parts and generates a dense shape which is used by the second module to estimate semantically and geometrically consistent keypoints. The approach also estimates confidence scores that allow the selection of valid keypoint considering the object's structure. We evaluate the proposed method for four different backbones and observe that we get better results using PointNet. Furthermore, the presented results show that the Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK) and Dual Alignment Score (DAS) for the keypoints estimated from the dense shapes (36.61 and 76.29) are 23.51 % and 12.14% higher, respectively, compared to those estimated from the partial objects (13.10 and 64.15).

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Approach for Frost Quantification in Domestic Refrigerators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Frost formation in refrigerators disrupts heat ex-change, lowering system efficiency and causing operational is-sues, making defrosting essential for maintaining performance. However, modern defrost systems rely on sensors for frost detection. The sensory approach is reliable but it could degrade over time in changing environmental conditions. To address this limitation, the paper proposes a real-time frost quantification method using digital image processing and deep learning. A custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is designed to classify frost thickness in RGB images captured inside a refrigerator. We have used a custom dataset, collected from a real refrigeration environment and made a comparison with other methods previously used for frost thickness estimation. The dataset is collected from several experiments to ensure its diversity such as illumination and environmental changes. This method enables precise frost detection, targeted for optimal defrost control for improved efficiency. Results indicate that the CNN model achieves a high test accuracy of 98.10%. The model's performance surpasses traditional methods, demonstrating its robustness in distinguishing varying frost levels from 0 to 4 (mm). This method enables precise frost thickness estimation and is a suitable choice for defrost control to improve the energy efficiency of the refrigerator.

articleTitle: Navigating the Maze Environment in ROS-2: An Experimental Comparison of Global and Local Planners for Dynamic Trajectory Planning in Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: A critical task in the quickly developing field of robotics is efficient path planning in dynamic environments. Within the framework of ROS2 (Robot Operating System 2), this paper gives a thorough comparative analysis of several autonomous mobile robot path planning algorithms, including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}^{*}$</tex>, Dijkstra, Regulated Pure Pursuit (RPP), and Dynamic Window Approach (DWA). This research investigated the effectiveness of merging local and global path planners in a dynamic maze environment using an experimental platform built on top of ROS2. Metrics include path length, deviation from the planned trajectory, and execution time. Obtained results demonstrate the performance of these algorithms highlighting their strengths and limitations while focusing on how some combinations perform better than others in terms of accuracy, planning time, and reliability.

articleTitle: Dynamic Temporal Modeling Using Cascaded Deep Networks and Encoder Transformers for Human Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Human action recognition is an important area of research in computer vision with its vast applications from healthcare to industrial environments, solving real-world problems like smart manufacturing, video surveillance, and artificial intelligence. The increased trends of human robot interactions in workplaces and everyday life further signify this area. Gesture-based control that helps a robot recognize motions, gestures, and other physical actions allows them to assist and operate seamlessly in various interactive settings by recognizing and responding to human actions in real-time. The human action recognition models require a very high computational power to process the video frames which usually comes with a lot of cost. This paper proposes a dynamic temporal modelling for effective spatio-temporal human action recognition by simultaneously capturing the short-term, long-term, and global contextual dependencies with a balanced trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) extract the spatial features, Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) efficiently handle the short-term patterns, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs) support the long-term temporal dependencies and transformers enhance global understanding. The cascaded architecture integrates EfficientNetB0 with LSTMs, GRUs and transformers to achieve a superior performance with computational efficiency. The proposed model outperforms benchmark dataset UCF50 achieving an accuracy of 92% and demonstrating improved inference time and robustness.

articleTitle: From Detection to Diagnosis: Elevating Track Fault Identification with Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: This paper presents a new application of transfer learning (TL) in improving the accuracy of track fault detection. Due to the diverse and complex nature of track faults it is hard to classify. There are various types of track faults such as Cracks, Flakings, Grooves, Joints, Shellings, Spallings, Squats. Classification of track fault could not be easily achieved using any simple machine learning (ML) algorithm. In this regard, this study uses pretrained models that are tuned to fit the peculiar nature of track fault. After acquiring track fault data from a widely cited repository of Mendeley from a research work already represented in ‘Data in Brief’. This application of TL achieves an unbeaten accuracy of 92%, which surpasses most previously generalized models with some explicit data augmentation strategies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach: Integrated Contextual Gate Networks for fNIRS-BCI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Brain Computer Interface (BCI) systems involve five stages: brain signal acquisition, signal preprocessing to remove artifacts, feature extraction, signal classification, and command generation for BCI application. Deep learning (DL) algorithms presents an important role in improving accuracy of functional near-infrared spectroscopy-BCI (fNIRS-BCI) systems. Like conventional machine learning (ML) classifiers, DL algorithms eliminate the necessity for manual feature extraction, as DL algorithms automatically recognize features and hidden patterns in the dataset for classification. In this study, we acquired a two-class motor activity dataset (Hand closing and opening) from twenty healthy participants. After preprocessing we applied z-score normalization on dataset to standardize the dataset and then DL integrated contextual gate network (ICGN) algorithm is used to enhance the classification accuracy of motor activity. The DL-ICGN network is designed to extract features from the preprocessed data to generate patterns based on the previously hidden cells information within the neural network, consequently classifying data based on these features and generated patterns. The DL-ICGN classification performance is compared with that of long short-term memory (LSTM) and bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) networks. The DL-ICGN algorithm attained a classification accuracy of 97.21 ± 0.73, significantly (p<0.025) outperforming the 89.72±2.85<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 94.02 ±1.73% accuracies of LSTM and Bi-LSTM, respectively. The results show that z-score normalization along with DL-ICGN classification algorithm can be successfully used for classifying both two-class and three-class classification problems in fNIRS-BCI systems applications.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of a Machine Learning Model for Cobot Action Prediction: Optimizing Algorithms Through Cognitive Workload Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI)
abstract: Collaborative robots (Cobots) have replaced traditional industrial robots on the factory floors, enhancing automation and efficiency. From the perspective of Industry 5.0, centering around H.F. (Human Factors), concerns about cognitive ergonomics persist as Cobots' unpredictable actions can increase cognitive workload and reduce productivity. Identifying and prioritising the operators' mental and physical well-being is necessary for safer and more efficient Human Robot Collaboration (HRC). This paper proposes a novel machine-learning model for Cobot action prediction and evaluates which algorithm is best for predicting Cobot actions based on operators' cognitive states. 75 participants with different levels of technophobia, technical expertise, and age collaborated with a Cobot to solve a complex maze puzzle. Firstly, each participant's Cognitive Workload (CWL) was measured using a combination of subjective and objective metrics (NASA-Task Load index, Heart Rate Variability, and Error Rate), followed by the development of a machine learning model that takes human factors as input parameters and predicts Cobot's actions accordingly. This study evaluates various machine learning models for Cobot action prediction and identifies that the Random Forest Classifier outperforms other models with an accuracy of 90%. The model can be implemented in various industrial settings to improve HRC safety and operators' cognitive ergonomics.
